content:
Hi all! I often want to inspect all the outputs of have?/apply?/rw?/simp?/suggestions?/try?/grind?/suggestions?/etc at once (without rerunning them).

Problem: successful/sorryful tactics affect the subsequent tactics. Using e.g. first | tac | ... or try recover [focus] tac mutates the context. I couldn't see a built-in tactic for cloning a goal.

Is there a way to do this using tactic combinators from Std+Batteries(+Mathlib)?
Yes! I don't have a mental model for which tactics subsume which, but I know it tends to subsume apply? without much extra cost

#help tactic hint

syntax "hint"... [Mathlib.Tactic.Hint.hintStx]
The hint tactic tries every tactic registered using register_hint <prio> tac,
and reports any that succeed.

and looking at the source, the calls are wrapped in an docs#Lean.observing?, so the starting state should be the same for each.
Oooh MonadBacktrack looks useful on its own merits
And aha, was not aware hint was directly configurable, ty all!

for posterity, it looks like hint is morally deprecated:
Kim Morrison said in #general > try? vs hint:

My intention is that hint is deprecated and will be removed, but this doesn't seem to have happened yet. Joachim is working on making try? even better, and there is already an extensibility mechanism to add library-defined tactics into try?.
